cards.headline: Google Reverses Search Ban After Educator Backlash
cards.hook: Google walked back a policy blocking student Search access in schools banning AI.
cards.tldr: Google initially proposed restricting student access to Google Search for any school district that implemented an artificial intelligence ban. This shift prompted a backlash from educators, as The New York Times reported, leading Google to reverse course. However, the company is proceeding with other aspects of the program, specifically allowing teachers to view transcripts of chatbot interactions on student accounts. While the access penalty has been removed, surveillance features remain active.
cards.memeLine: Google tried to hold Search hostage for AI adoption and blinked first.

cards.headline: CrowdStrike’s AI Kill Switch: A Brake for Rogue Agents
cards.hook: George Kurtz unveils a tool to stop AI misbehavior in its tracks.
cards.tldr: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz announced an AI kill switch designed to halt rogue internal agents. Built into the Falcon Guardian platform launched in September, the feature aims to curb misbehavior while preserving innovation. While the capability addresses a real risk of autonomous systems acting unpredictably, current evidence is limited to the vendor's announcement. It remains unproven whether this specific mechanism will effectively distinguish between dangerous deviations and necessary operational adjustments in live enterprise environments without causing collateral disruption to critical workflows.
cards.memeLine: Finally, a circuit breaker for the digital mind.

cards.headline: OpenAI Retires ChatGPT Classic App in 2027
cards.hook: The old app is leaving. The new one is coming.
cards.tldr: OpenAI has announced that the standalone ChatGPT Classic app will be retired on January 30, 2027. Users opening the app now see a banner confirming this date. The company plans to combine the Chat and Work tabs into a single new application. Codex will remain a separate experience within the ChatGPT desktop app. This consolidation marks a significant shift in how users access OpenAI's core services, moving away from distinct mobile applications toward a unified ecosystem. The change affects millions of daily users who rely on the classic interface for quick interactions.

cards.headline: Anthropic Blocks Claude From Recreating Video Games
cards.hook: Claude now refuses to generate recreations of existing games, following legal pressure.
cards.tldr: Anthropic has updated Claude to prevent users from generating AI recreations of their favorite video games. This restriction follows a $1.5 billion settlement with authors and an Elvis Presley estate lawsuit. The change limits creative tools but avoids new litigation risks. Users can still build original content, but cannot replicate protected works directly through the model.
cards.memeLine: Claude is no longer your game dev assistant.

cards.headline: Anthropic blocks Claude from reverse-engineering game code
cards.hook: Claude now restricts modding and decompiling, limiting user access to legacy code tools.
cards.tldr: Anthropic has quietly updated its usage policies to block Claude from performing work such as modding, decompiling, or reverse-engineering video game code. This restriction applies to both Claude Code and specific model versions like Opus 5.5, affecting users attempting to recreate games using tools like Reverse Engineer Anything. The move coincides with the introduction of a Cyber Verification Program that limits advanced cybersecurity capabilities to entities covered by Project Glasswing. While some speculate Adobe is behind this shift, the primary impact is on developers relying on AI for non-malicious generic reverse engineering tasks. This change effectively closes off a previously available avenue for code analysis and game preservation efforts.
cards.memeLine: The AI lawyer just told you to stop reading the source code.
